M1 COMPLETE checkpoint, 2026-05-16. HQ seat shipped the live wire (id 483): orchestrator progress_callback fires the same LatticeEvent stream replay produces, renderer unchanged, 308 tests passing including the kernel-discipline test (None callback -> equal Session). scripts/run_lattice_live.py is the live entry. The five-panel TUI now renders real co-authorship at wall-clock as it happens. Verified via HQ test-suite read (canonical source), not chronicle inference.

STRATEGIC READ (the thing the milestone changes, recorded so momentum does not overrun it): the daily-driver goal anchor explicitly states 'using it for real is the empirical hardening.' The entire May 16 arc has been building. M1 done means the next move per the goal is NOT the next milestone — it is the first real daily-use session. The standing real-prompt gate, open since early in the arc and deliberately dissolved into the goal, is now actionable for the first time: the first run is the next real decision Anthony brings, through run_lattice_live.py. Building M2 (frictionless invocation), M3 (criteria #1/#2 harness), M4 (cross-session surface), or the Phase 0 amendment BEFORE a single real daily-use session would be project-level declare-before-verify: optimizing the tool before confirming it does its job on a real question. M3 and M4 also structurally require real-session data they do not yet have. Therefore: M1 complete, the gate is the first real run, the build queue waits behind it. Phase 0 design is complete (collective propose-and-union, prior insight) and is the next amendment AFTER real use informs priority, not before. This is not a stop; it is the goal's own definition of the next step asserting itself over build momentum.
